fields.slugAuto: Made from the name when empty

aggregates.title: Aggregates and RIRs
aggregates.hint: An aggregate is a top-level block of address space assigned by a registry (a RIR, or a standard such as RFC 1918). Aggregates never overlap. Utilization is the share of the block covered by prefixes of any routing table.
aggregates.required: The prefix and the RIR are required.
aggregates.prefixHint: IPv4 or IPv6 network with its mask. It may not overlap another aggregate.
aggregates.deleteConfirm: Delete the aggregate {name}? The prefixes inside it are kept.

rirs.privateHint: Private (the space managed by this registry is private, for example RFC 1918)

asns.title: ASNs
asns.hint: Autonomous system numbers (16 or 32 bit, written 65000 or in ASDOT notation 1.10) and the ranges of AS numbers a registry handed out.
asns.required: The AS number and the RIR are required.
asns.rangeRequired: Name, RIR, start and end are required.
asns.asnHint: A number from 1 to 4294967295, or ASDOT such as 1.10.
asns.deleteRangeConfirm: Delete the ASN range {name}? The ASNs inside it are kept.
asns.freeCount: {n} free AS number(s). The first ones:
asns.sitesHint: The sites that operate this AS number.

import.title: Import IP addresses from asset interfaces
import.hint: Reads the IP addresses typed on the network interfaces of the assets and creates an IPAM address for each, assigned to that interface. The mask comes from the address, from the subnet mask of the interface, or is a single host. Nothing on the assets changes, and running it again skips what is already imported. Look at the preview first.
import.perSiteHint: Plants often reuse the same private addresses. With this on, each site gets its own VRF (named after the site, created when missing) so the same address can exist in several sites. Assets without a site use the VRF above.
import.createPrefixes: Also create the network of each address (for example 10.0.0.0/24)
import.done: Imported: {created} created, {linked} linked to existing addresses, {prefixes} prefix(es) created.
import.nothing: No address is typed on any asset interface.
import.truncated: Only the first rows are listed; the import covers all of them.

prefixes.title: Prefixes
prefixes.hint: The address space: IPv4 and IPv6 networks, nested by routing table. Utilization counts the IP addresses and ranges inside each prefix (a container counts its child prefixes).
prefixes.prefixHint: IPv4 or IPv6 network with its mask. Host bits are cleared (10.0.0.5/24 is saved as 10.0.0.0/24).
prefixes.deleteConfirm: Delete the prefix {name}? The prefixes and addresses inside it are kept.

fields.isPool: Is a pool (every address is usable)

addresses.title: IP addresses
addresses.hint: Individual addresses with their mask. An address can be assigned to an interface of an asset; the interface details on the asset are not changed.
addresses.allocateHint: The lowest free address of {prefix} is taken.
addresses.searchPlaceholder: Search address, DNS name or description
addresses.addressHint: IPv4 or IPv6 address with its mask, for example 10.0.0.5/24.
addresses.assignHint: Optional. Network IDs and broadcast addresses cannot be assigned to an interface.
addresses.fhrpHint: Optional. Makes this a virtual address shared by the group (the role follows the protocol). An address is assigned to an interface or to a group, not both.

ranges.title: IP ranges
ranges.hint: A run of addresses from a start to an end. Ranges in the same routing table cannot overlap. A range marked populated blocks new addresses inside it.
ranges.required: The start and end addresses are required.

fields.markPopulated: Mark populated (no addresses may be created inside)

vlans.title: VLANs
vlans.hint: VLAN IDs 1-4094. A VLAN group holds ID ranges; inside a group the VLAN ID and name must be unique.
vlans.required: The VLAN ID and name are required.
vlans.deleteConfirm: Delete the VLAN {name}? Prefixes that use it are kept.
vlans.rangesHint: Allowed VLAN IDs, for example 1-99, 200-299, 500. Empty means 1-4094.
vlans.svlanRequired: A customer VLAN needs a service VLAN.

vrfs.title: VRFs and roles
vrfs.hint: A VRF is a separate routing table; prefixes and addresses without a VRF are in the global table. Roles describe the function of a prefix, range or VLAN.
vrfs.deleteRoleConfirm: Delete the role {name}? Prefixes, ranges and VLANs that use it are kept.
vrfs.enforceHint: Refuses duplicate prefixes and addresses inside this VRF.

routeTargets.hint: BGP route targets (RFC 4364) decide which routes a VRF imports and exports, for example 65000:100.
routeTargets.deleteConfirm: Delete the route target {name}? VRFs that use it are kept.
routeTargets.vrfHint: Route targets are created on the Route targets tab.

fhrp.title: FHRP groups
fhrp.hint: First hop redundancy groups (VRRP, HSRP, GLBP, CARP ...): a group shares virtual IP addresses between the interfaces of several assets. Assign the virtual addresses on the IP address form.
fhrp.searchPlaceholder: Search name, group ID or description
fhrp.deleteConfirm: Delete {name}? Its services and interface assignments are deleted; its virtual addresses are kept.
fhrp.noAddresses: No virtual address is assigned to this group.
fhrp.addressHint: Assigned on the IP address form.
fhrp.noInterfaces: No interface takes part in this group.

services.title: Services
services.hint: A service is a name with TCP, UDP or SCTP ports, offered by an asset or by an FHRP group, optionally on some of its IP addresses. Templates hold the usual combinations (for example Web: tcp/80, tcp/443).
services.required: The name and the ports are required.
services.parentRequired: Choose the asset or the FHRP group that offers the service.
services.portsHint: Protocol and port, separated by commas: tcp/80, udp/53, tcp/8000-8010.
services.addressesHint: Optional. Leave empty if the service is not tied to particular addresses.
services.deleteTemplateConfirm: Delete the template {name}? Services made from it are kept.

csv.hint: Use the file of the export as the model: export, edit it in a spreadsheet (save as CSV UTF-8, comma or semicolon), and import it. Names (VRF, role, site, VLAN group, asset) are used instead of IDs. Look at the preview first; nothing is written until you import.

columns.prefixes: prefix, vrf, status, role, vlan_group, vlan_vid, site, is_pool, mark_utilized, description
columns.addresses: address, vrf, status, role, dns_name, asset (tag or name), interface, fhrp_protocol, fhrp_group, description
columns.vlans: vid, name, group, status, site, role, description

csv.updateExisting: Update the ones that already exist
csv.updateHint: A row that matches an existing object (same prefix and VRF, same address and VRF, same VLAN ID and group) replaces it, blank cells included. Without this they are skipped.
csv.skipInvalid: Import the valid rows even if some rows are invalid
csv.invalidBlocks: Some rows are invalid, so nothing will be imported unless you tick "Import the valid rows even if some rows are invalid".

translation.hint: A policy is a named set of rules that translate a local VLAN ID to a remote one. Apply it to an interface from the interface IPAM settings on the asset page.
translation.ruleRequired: The local and remote VLAN IDs are required.
translation.deleteConfirm: Delete the policy {name} and its rules?

interfaceSettings.title: IPAM settings of {name}
interfaceSettings.hint: Routing table, VLAN mode and VLANs of this interface. The IP address, mask and VLAN text typed on the interface are not changed.

assetAddresses.title: Primary addresses
assetAddresses.hint: Choose among the IPAM addresses assigned to the interfaces of this asset. An address can be primary for one asset only.
assetAddresses.none: No IPAM address is assigned to an interface of this asset yet.
